plan_summary: Install and configure Nginx on Ubuntu 24.04 by updating system packages, adding the official repository key if necessary, installing the package, verifying the service status, and configuring basic security settings.
assumptions: The host is a fresh or standard Ubuntu 24.04 installation with network access.
Sudo privileges are available for the executing user.
No specific custom Nginx configuration files are required beyond defaults.

tasks.title: Update System Package Index
tasks.objective: Ensure the local package index is current to fetch the latest Nginx version and dependencies.
tasks.rationale: Running apt update before installation prevents installing outdated packages and ensures compatibility with Ubuntu 24.04 repositories.
tasks.expected_output: Command completes successfully with a summary of updated package lists.
success_criteria: No critical errors reported during update.

tasks.title: Verify Nginx Repository Availability
tasks.objective: Check if the default Ubuntu repositories contain the required Nginx package version.
tasks.rationale: Ubuntu 24.04 includes Nginx in its main repositories; this step confirms availability before attempting installation to avoid unnecessary key additions.
tasks.expected_output: Output showing the installed or available version of Nginx and its source repository.
success_criteria: Nginx is listed as a package available in 'main' or 'universe'.

tasks.title: Install Nginx Package
tasks.objective: Download and install the Nginx web server software and its dependencies.
tasks.rationale: This is the core installation step that places binaries, libraries, and default configuration files onto the system.
tasks.expected_output: Nginx package installed with a summary of new/updated packages.

tasks.title: Start and Enable Nginx Service
tasks.objective: Launch the Nginx daemon and configure it to start automatically on boot.
tasks.rationale: Installation alone does not run the service; systemd commands are required to manage the process lifecycle.

tasks.title: Verify Web Server Accessibility
tasks.objective: Confirm the web server is responding to HTTP requests on port 80.
tasks.rationale: Functional verification ensures that the installation and service start were successful and the firewall allows traffic.
tasks.expected_output: HTML content from the default Nginx welcome page or a valid HTTP 200 response.

tasks.title: Review Default Configuration Files
tasks.objective: Inspect the contents of /etc/nginx/sites-available/default and other config directories.
tasks.rationale: Understanding the default configuration helps identify potential security risks or misconfigurations before production use.
tasks.expected_output: Listed content of key Nginx configuration files including server blocks.
success_criteria: Configuration syntax is valid (no obvious errors in default file).

tasks.title: Configure Basic Security Headers
tasks.objective: Add security headers (e.g., X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy) to the default site configuration.
tasks.rationale: Default Nginx configurations often lack essential security headers; adding them mitigates common web vulnerabilities.
tasks.expected_output: Updated configuration file with added 'add_header' directives.
success_criteria: Security headers are present in the config file.

tasks.title: Reload Nginx Configuration
tasks.objective: Apply the security header changes without interrupting active connections.
tasks.rationale: Changes to configuration files must be reloaded for the server to recognize them.
tasks.expected_output: Confirmation message that the reload was successful.
success_criteria: Reload command completes with exit code 0.

tasks.title: Verify Security Headers Implementation
tasks.objective: Confirm that the newly added security headers are present in HTTP responses.
tasks.rationale: Validation ensures that the configuration changes in T07 and T08 were applied correctly.
tasks.expected_output: HTTP response headers containing X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, etc.
success_criteria: Response headers include the defined security directives.

tasks.title: Document Installation Steps
tasks.objective: Create a brief summary of the installation process and current configuration state.
tasks.rationale: Documentation aids in future maintenance, troubleshooting, or replication on other hosts.
tasks.expected_output: A text file or note containing version info, config paths, and verification results.
success_criteria: Document exists and contains relevant installation details.
